properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on 0.76.0, 0.78.0 and 0.79.0): every one-shot open (--call, read, write, --export, --import, --diff) drops the version verdict. It prints no 'Additive only' notice, not even on stderr, never sets served_by.behind_record, and rewrites graph.meta.json, down as well as up. The repair report reaches loop_status only when the opening process's own call is loop_status. Only the --shared daemon's stderr is a file, which is why only those sessions left notices in graph.server.log
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-05, triaging art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05: entry [gap] (lines 376-387), and the idea in entry [works] (lines 350-354).

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "the 0.79.0 upgrade recipe's step 3 ('first open should say the store was written by 0.76.0 … additive only') could not be confirmed after the fact. Earlier notices (0.70→0.73→0.74→0.75→0.76 ...) are in `.reflow2/graph.server.log` because they came from `--serve` sessions; under `--call` / `reflow2 read` the notice goes to that one process's stderr and nowhere else, and `graph.meta.json` is rewritten to `0.79.0` on that open. No 0.79.0 line exists in any of the 20 stores' logs." Of the repair: "the repair's report went to the first opener and was not visible later". NOT AFFECTED: the store opens, and nothing in it is lost.

② PRECEDENT: fact:root-cause-an-upgrade-under-a-session-is-known-at-open-and-said-only-to-stderr-2026-09-28. The verdict is computed at every open, and only the NewerWriter case reaches served_by. Its class: open-time facts leave only through a log no session reads. fact:root-cause-one-shot-modes-return-before-the-pointer-check-and-opening-a-store-creates-it-2026-10-02 has the same shape: the one-shot modes skip what the server's open path does.

③ CANDIDATES:
(A) the door prints the notice on stderr, and nobody keeps it (the reporter's reading).
(B) the door does not print it at all.
(C) only some serving modes write graph.server.log.
(D) the observation is wrong, and the notice can be recovered from somewhere else.

④⑤ MEASURED. A scratch store written by 0.74.0 was opened with 0.79.0 four ways: `reflow2 read graph_report`, `reflow2 read loop_status`, `--call loop_status` with RUST_LOG unset, and `--export`.
- None of the four printed a "written by" line on stderr. Each printed only the INFO "opening" line. graph.meta.json read 0.79.0 afterwards in every case. 0.76.0 through `--call` behaves the same. ⇒ (A) REFUTED, (B) HOLDS.
- CODE (main at 7f5984ec5). The door's opener `open_the_design` (main.rs) calls `ReflowService::new`. That calls `DesignGraph::open_rocksdb`, which is `open_rocksdb_with_provenance(path)?.0`, so the verdict is dropped. `--export`, `--export-snapshot`, `--import` and `--diff` call `open_rocksdb` directly. Only `new_reporting` keeps the note, and only the serving modes call it: `ServeAs::prepare` prints it with tracing::warn and eprintln.
- The stdio server prints the notice on its stderr, which is the harness's log. The `--shared` client starts a daemon whose stderr IS `.reflow2/graph.server.log`, so the notice lands there. ⇒ (C) HOLDS. The reporter's earlier notices came from shared daemons.
- THE DOWNGRADE CASE BEHAVES THE SAME, AND IT IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. A store stamped 0.79.0 was opened with 0.78.0. On stdio, 0.78.0 prints "THIS GRAPH WAS LAST WRITTEN BY reflow2 0.79.0 ... BEHIND it" and serves served_by.behind_record. Through `--call loop_status` it prints nothing, served_by has no behind_record, and graph.meta.json is rewritten down to 0.78.0. The guard built on 2026-09-15 for writes by a binary behind its record does not exist on the door.
- THE REPAIR REPORT. The 0.74.0 store's first 0.79.0 open repairs 2 retired values. When that open is `read loop_status`, the reply carries `repaired_on_open`. When it is `read graph_report` or `--export`, the repair happens and is reported nowhere, and no later loop_status carries `repaired_on_open`. So CHANGELOG 0.75.0's "Nothing is repaired silently" is false on these doors.
- (D) HOLDS IN PART. `<graph>.usage.jsonl` records `client_version` on every door call (client "reflow2-mcp --call": 0.74.0, then 0.79.0). So on a door-only store, which version used it and when that changed CAN be read afterwards. The verdict, the type counts and any repair cannot.

⑥ CLASS: as on 2026-09-28, facts computed once at open leave only through a process's own log. On the one-shot doors there is not even that, and the door is what a VS Code machine uses for everything. So it hears none of the three open-time verdicts: older, newer, unstamped. The class-level fix the 09-28 walk named (keep the verdict and serve it) would have covered this report too. A fix only at the log would not have reached the downgrade case. It also meets dec:backup-belongs-to-the-consumer part (3), which says "We opened a store an older binary wrote and said nothing" is not a fair thing for a tool to do.

⑦ NOT BUILT. A test pinning the class would open two stores through `--call`, one stamped older and one stamped newer. It would assert that the reply or stderr names the other version, and that a newer stamp is not rewritten down without a word.

COORDINATION: fix/a-stores-identity-follows-its-real-path (another agent, 2026-10-05, not merged when this was written) is rewriting `open_rocksdb_with_provenance` so that a refused open writes nothing. It keeps an `identity_on_open` note for loop_status, the way repaired_on_open is kept, and says it on stderr. A fix here touches the same function. It belongs after that branch merges, and should follow its pattern. Idea: dec:idea-what-the-first-open-after-an-upgrade-found-outlives-the-process-that-opened.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: the field machine's own timeline (which tool opened each store first after 11:55). Whether `reflow2 read`'s promise that it "changes nothing" should cover the open's restamp and repair is a question for the owner, and was not measured here.
